Q: Can docker network be specified for local docker deployment in Skaffold? A:

Yes, you can specify a Docker network for Skaffold's local Docker deployment on different ways.

Using skaffold.yaml

You can specify the network in your skaffold.yaml configuration

apiVersion: skaffold/v4beta9
kind: Config
build:
  artifacts:
    - image: my-app
      docker:
        dockerfile: Dockerfile
deploy:
  docker:
    network: my-network  # <-- Specify your network here
    containers:
      - name: my-app
        image: my-app
        ports:
          - containerPort: 8080
            hostPort: 8080

For multiple containers

Use the containers field

apiVersion: skaffold/v4beta9
kind: Config
deploy:
  docker:
    containers:
      - name: app1
        image: app1
        network: my-custom-network  # Network for this specific container
        ports:
          - containerPort: 8080
      - name: app2
        image: app2
        network: my-custom-network  # Same network for both containers

Using Docker Compose with Skaffold

If you need more complex networking, you can use the hybrid Docker Compose with Skaffold:

# skaffold.yaml
apiVersion: skaffold/v4beta9
kind: Config
deploy:
  dockerCompose:
    files:
      - docker-compose.yaml

# docker-compose.yaml
version: '3.8'
services:
  my-app:
    build: .
    network_mode: "bridge"
    networks:
      - my-network
    ports:
      - "8080:8080"
  database:
    image: postgres:14
    networks:
      - my-network
    environment:
      POSTGRES_PASSWORD: password

networks:
  my-network:
    external: true  # Use existing network
    name: bridge    # Or your existing network name

Connecting containers to existing network

If you can't specify the network directly, you can:

  1. Connect existing containers to your network: 
    docker network connect bridge my-existing-database
  2. Or run skaffold with an existing database in the same network by starting them together in a compose file.

Note: Make sure the network exists before running Skaffold. I will assume you got that one.

Q: How can I set an environment variable in a Qt *.pro file? A:

You can set default environment variables for each kit. You don't need to regenerate the .pro or .pro.user file for it to happen. When you add the definition, it'll make it available to the project automatically.

Just go to Tools | Options | Kits and select your kit. Then, scroll down to where it has the Environment label on the left, and a "Change" button on the right. Click it. Then, paste MAKEFLAGS=-j4 in that window. If you then close out of preferences and go to Projects and select the "Build" entry for your compiler on the left, and scroll down to your Build Environment at right, you'll find it there. Then, every project you make with that toolset will have the environment variable. Of course, you'll have to redefine it every time you update the compiler.
